candidate: Fixed-reference two-score conditional conformal test martingale (x and x^2) with union-bounded alpha/delta budgets plus an early t/F sentinel

grade.finite_delay_certificate_at_n_684: C+/not derived beyond positive-signal condition and theorem-order bound

published_claim_and_official_support.paper: Shaer, Bar, Prinster & Romano (2026), Testing For Distribution Shifts with Conditional Conformal Test Martingales, arXiv:2602.13848v2 / ICML 2026.
published_claim_and_official_support.method_scope: The paper explicitly treats a fixed finite calibration/reference sample and an indefinitely growing test stream. It forms a calibration ECDF, subtracts a DKW confidence-band correction in its robust betting function, and provides anytime conditional type-I control on the calibration-good event together with asymptotic-power / expected-delay order results when the effective signal is positive.

official_repository.implementation_support: cond_ctm.py keeps a fixed calibration ECDF, computes the DKW band, applies the confidence-adjusted betting score and updates the betting parameter by ONS. utils.py implements epsilon=sqrt(log(2/delta)/(2n)) and the confidence-adjusted bet. requirements.txt pins the Python package environment.
official_repository.reproducibility_limit: No tagged release/exact paper-code freeze was established in this audit. Current main postdates arXiv v2, so the present repository head should not be silently equated with the exact paper execution snapshot.

formula_checks: For score s1(x)=x under X~N(0,1), Y~N(mu,r), E[Phi(Y)] = Phi(mu/sqrt(1+r)); therefore the worker signal a(mu,r)=Phi(|mu|/sqrt(1+r))-1/2 is correct.
For score s2(x)=x^2, the population ECDF mean equals P(X^2 <= Y^2)=P(|X| <= |Y|), so b(mu,r)=|P(|Y|>|X|)-1/2| is the corresponding continuous-distribution signal.

reproduced_minimax_point.note: Independent global numerical optimization reproduced the worker's reported minimizer and floor to displayed precision. A broader constrained search over mu in [0,15] and r in [1e-6,100] with KL>=1 again returned the same neighborhood. This is strong numerical reproduction, not a continuum proof.

dkw_and_budget_reproduction.type_i_budget_reasoning: On each channel's DKW-good event, the calibration ECDF can move the population PIT mean by at most epsilon, and the conditional-CTM robust bet pays another epsilon in the effective signal. Hence Delta_0 is lower bounded by population_signal-2*epsilon. Separately, two per-channel rejection probabilities at alpha=0.02 plus two calibration-band failures at delta=0.005 union-bound to 0.05; no channel independence is needed.

independent_external_reproduction_search.lead: A Hugging Face Space named SabaPivot/repro-testing-for-distribution-shifts-with-conditional-conformal-test-martingales was located, but this audit did not obtain enough immutable code/result detail to verify it as a protocol-matched independent reproduction. It is retained only as an unverified reproduction lead.
independent_external_reproduction_search.scope_rule: Do not count the Space as independent replication until its code, data/model pins, run protocol and numerical outputs can be inspected and matched.

scope_corrections_and_limits: The worker's two-score Gaussian construction is an adaptation of the published conditional-CTM method, not an author-demonstrated configuration from the paper.
The independently reproduced 0.16437289881 floor is numerical. No interval/direct-rounding or analytic proof over the entire KL>=1 continuum was produced in this audit.

The paper's power theorem requires a positive calibration-conditional effective signal. The DKW-good event plus population_signal>2*epsilon provides a meaningful route to Delta_0>0 for fixed score maps, but this audit did not derive a sharp finite expected-delay constant at n=684 beyond the theorem's order statement.

The fixed-score assumption matters. If Gaussian centering/scaling parameters are learned from the same reference observations used to calibrate the ECDF, the published guarantee must not be transferred without a separate argument. External fixed scores or a fit/calibration split is the safer generic construction.
No matched common-random-path delay/power comparison against the existing t/F sentinel or SNML future-tail channel was executed here.
verdict: The core fixed-reference conditional-CTM mechanism and the worker's algebra/budget arithmetic are strongly supported. The most important new result is independent reproduction of the two-score minimax numerical floor and the DKW-adjusted positive-signal margin. The candidate is therefore materially stronger than a speculative idea, but the headline all-Gaussian KL>=1 guarantee remains unproved until the numerical floor is continuum-certified and the fixed-score/standardization contract is made explicit.
reopen_or_next_evidence: Provide an interval-certified or analytic proof of inf_{KL>=1} max{a(mu,r),b(mu,r)} >= a robust constant near 0.1643, including radial extension beyond the KL=1 boundary.
Translate the certified floor through the exact Shaer-et-al. ONS/betting constants at n=684, alpha=0.02, delta=0.005 to obtain an explicit finite delay certificate, not only asymptotic/big-O support.
Run a matched common-random Gaussian comparison versus the current t/F sentinel and SNML future-tail channel under one global PFA budget.
For unknown baseline mean/variance, specify and test an independent fit/calibration split and account for the smaller calibration sample.
Inspect the independent reproduction lead only if immutable code/protocol/results can be obtained; do not upgrade replication status from name/metadata alone.
